page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head and page number at the top (title left, number 345 right). Text continues below. A centred "X." sits between two paragraphs. At the foot: signature "P 5" at left and catchword "eof-" at right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Idque suadet ratio: est enim defensio juris naturae, quod omnibus hominibus est commune: adeoque in quo omnes sunt pares; sic ut hominem homini insidiari propter natura-lem cognationem nefas sit. Init. Inst. jur. nat. Gent. Civil. Init. Inst. de libertin. l. 9. D. de Just. & Jur. l. 3. eod. Etiam id suadet genera-litas l. 2. Cod. Ad l. Corn. de Si-car. junctâ l. 3. Cod. eod. l. 3. D. just. & jur. Quae leges cùm nemi-nem excipiant, neque quem-piam excipere nobis licebit. Erubescimus enim sine lege loqui. Novell. 18. cap. 5. Gail. 2. Observ. 110. n. 12.

In specie quaeritur an Eccle-siasticae personae, moderamen inculpatae tu[?]telae rectè adhibe-ant? Respondeo nec illis id denegari posse. Homines enim sunt, communi naturae neces-sitati obstricti; ut æquum sit

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "tu[?]telae" (the letter after "tu" is unclear, possibly "te" or "tu" with a dot); catchword "eof-" is read from a small line at the foot and may be "eos-" [?]. Long s was printed throughout and is transcribed as plain s (e.g. "fuadet" as "suadet", "fine" as "sine", "fit" as "sit"). The reference lines in italics are printed inline in the text block, not as margin notes. The first paragraph continues from the previous page.
